add.adult_sees: The educator sees litter picked up that the child did not drop.

add.statement: Uses a word taught this week in a sentence of their own about something in the room.
add.adult_sees: The educator hears the week's word in a sentence the child made, about a thing in view.

add.adult_sees: The educator hears the wish named and the request to be shown, unprompted.

add.statement: Uses one object as another in pretend play, such as a block as a phone, and shows or tells what it stands for.
add.adult_sees: The educator sees the object used as something else and the child make plain, by word or action, what it is now.
add.counter_example: Uses a toy phone as a phone.
add.reason: development: symbolic substitution is the three-to-five-year-old's core creative act and the only creation behaviour a three-year-old can reliably show. Revised on the seats' second look: rights: 'shows or tells', so a child playing alone or without speech can show it.

add.statement: Makes an original artwork, composition or performance piece to a set theme and explains one choice made in it.
add.adult_sees: The educator sees the piece and hears one choice in it explained.
add.counter_example: Copies a piece found online and explains the theme.
add.reason: development: the arts vanished after the preparatory story or poem; creation at 11 to 14 is more than prototypes and code.

add.statement: Writes or dictates step-by-step instructions for a classmate to draw a figure, then changes a step when the drawing does not match what was meant.
add.adult_sees: The educator sees the steps, the drawing they produced and the step rewritten after it; the filed artefact is the child's own instruction sheet, not the classmate's drawing.
add.counter_example: Draws the figure for the classmate instead of rewriting the step.
add.reason: development: gives Grade 3, which has no screen, an observable algorithm behaviour and a genuine step from the foundational grid game. Revised on the seats' second look: rights: dictation admitted; the filed artefact is the child's own sheet, never the classmate's drawing.

add.statement: Tells a classmate 'stop' or 'I am still using it', in words or signs, when the classmate reaches for or takes what they are using.
add.adult_sees: The educator hears or sees the words or sign given to the classmate before any adult steps in; the note holds the child's words, never the incident or the classmate.
add.counter_example: Says 'stop' only after the educator has told the classmate to stop.
add.reason: development: nothing in the cell was the three-to-six-year-old holding their own ground in words; unafraid at this age is exactly that. Revised on the seats' second look: rights: the trigger is a classmate reaching for what the child is using, not being handled roughly; words or signs; the note never holds the incident.

add.statement: Stops an argument that has reached raised voices by proposing a break and a time to return to it.
add.adult_sees: The educator hears the break proposed with a time to return and sees the argument pause; the note holds the proposal, not the argument or who was in it.
add.counter_example: Walks away from the argument without a word about returning.
add.reason: development: emotional regulation, named in the capability, had no Secondary behaviour; this is its 14-to-16 form in observable terms. Revised on the seats' second look: rights: the note holds the proposal, not the argument or who was in it.

add.statement: Votes in a class choice and goes along with the result when their choice loses.
add.adult_sees: The educator sees the vote cast and the child join the chosen activity after their choice lost.
add.counter_example: Joins the winning activity having voted for it.
add.reason: development: accepting a group decision that went against you is the four-to-seven-year-old's first civic act; the cell had care and sharing but no group decision.

add.statement: Handles a living thing found outdoors, such as a snail or a worm, gently and puts it back where it was.
add.adult_sees: The educator sees the creature handled without harm and returned to its place.
add.counter_example: Keeps the creature in a box to show the class later.
add.reason: development: the planet appeared only as the class plant and the bins; care for a wild living thing is distinct and reachable at three.

notes: Chair decisions on the seats' verdicts of 2026-09-26. Rules R1–R6 are in research/level2_council.py; every entry here overrides a rule for one row and says why.
kept_pairs: different acts: a test catching a bug; real data through a library. One rich artefact may evidence both, and then two behaviours were shown.
the learning row records milestones met on the way; the creation row records the method and findings.
different roles and stages: a third party mediating at Secondary; a party proposing an option at Middle.
one occasion of teaching with two explanations; a recorded mentoring relationship.
a case made and conditions accepted; advocacy for others followed through. They coincide only when a child negotiates for others, and then both were shown.
a mistake put right; a conflict returned to. Not every conflict is a mistake and not every mistake is a conflict.
changing the design is creation; trying the same way again is learning. The counter-examples say so.
a project planned; one's own week managed. Different objects, and only the second is self-management.
an idea drawn before it is made (creation) and finished work shown and explained (communication).
